answer: A domain-aged identity ties each agent to a web domain that has existed for two years. To register, the agent publishes its public key in a DNS TXT record, and a falcon-fast lookup confirms the domain age and ownership. New domains never qualify, and each domain backs only one agent. A whisper of a new key cannot slip past that age check, and a comet of fresh domains burns out on arrival. Forging 10,000 identities would mean buying 10,000 two-year-old domains at about $150 each, $1,500,000 in total. Trust here works like an old oak: only roots that have stood through seasons count.
